quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2026 Financial Results Briefing Q&A (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Hiroshi Nishio (results briefing Q&A, quarter to June 2026): MHI received orders for ten large frame gas turbines in Q1 - four for the United States and six for Japan; the Americas projects include long-term service agreements, while in Japan after-sales services are generally contracted separately each year. Demand in the Americas is extremely strong, order pricing has not declined and the profitability of newly booked projects keeps improving gradually; with its core US utility customers MHI is selective about the projects it contracts, and there has been no change in the strong supply-demand environment. Q1 orders are generally scheduled for delivery between 2028 and 2030, while projects now under discussion would generally deliver around 2030 to 2031. Full-year GTCC order intake forecast was raised by JPY 100 billion on continued strong demand, particularly in North America, not on any single large award.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1: 10 large frame gas turbine orders (4 US, 6 Japan); GTCC order forecast raised by JPY 100 billion; deliveries 2028-2030

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2026 Financial Results Briefing Q&A (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Hiroshi Nishio (results briefing Q&A): demand for large frame gas turbines remains broadly in line with, or slightly above, the strong level MHI anticipated, and the production-capacity expansion needed to meet it is progressing smoothly; but capacity being expected to double in the future does not mean MHI is immediately seeking to book twice as many orders - it builds the order book while monitoring the expansion and confirming how much added capacity can come on stream with sufficient certainty.
quarterly_data.figure: production capacity expected to double in the future

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2026 Financial Results Briefing Q&A (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Hiroshi Nishio (results briefing Q&A): Q1 one-time items totalled approximately JPY 25 billion, mostly in Energy Systems - around JPY 15 billion of profit recognised when the contract price of an exceptionally large, long-term plant construction project was finalised (the revenue adjustment was greater than JPY 15 billion; similar gains are not expected often) and approximately JPY 10 billion of gains on the sale of investments in several power generation projects, including a South American project invested in to secure an MHI gas turbine order, plus onshore wind and solar. Even excluding these, the Energy Systems business profit margin exceeded the full-year assumption, so there may be some upside to full-year guidance. No tariff refunds contributed; the profitability of original-equipment orders, particularly for the US, has improved significantly, and the margin is expected to improve gradually as higher-margin orders are recognised as revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: one-time items approximately JPY 25 billion (JPY 15 billion contract-price finalisation; JPY 10 billion gains on sale of project investments)

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries results briefing Q&A: Q1 FY2026 Financial Results Briefing Q&A (08-06-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Hiroshi Nishio (results briefing Q&A): the full-year Defense order intake forecast was raised by approximately JPY 100 billion after reviewing Q1 progress, not on any specific new project. Defense order intake has been approximately JPY 1.5 trillion annually for the past three years and is forecast at approximately JPY 1.5 trillion this fiscal year after the revision; revenue is expected to rise gradually toward that level, so MHI is investing in facilities and expanding production capacity, with more detail in the next medium-term business plan. The full-year free cash flow forecast was raised mainly because GTCC advances received increased more than expected, and also on timing changes of certain major investment projects; MHI is formulating its 2027 Medium-Term Business Plan and will explain its capital allocation approach once that is complete.
quarterly_data.figure: Defense orders forecast approximately JPY 1.5 trillion (raised by approximately JPY 100 billion)
